title: AI Governance Evidence Pack for Banks
summary: Inventory the bank's AI and ML systems and assemble the evidence boards, auditors and supervisors ask for: purpose, data, testing, monitoring, incidents and accountable owners.

seo.title: AI Governance Evidence Pack for Banks | VipraTech
seo.description: Inventory your bank's AI systems and assemble evidence on data, testing, monitoring and ownership, aligned with RBI FREE-AI, ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF.

problem.intro: Most banks now run AI in more places than anyone has listed: credit scorecards, fraud models, chatbots, document extraction, vendor tools with embedded models and staff use of general-purpose assistants. Boards and auditors increasingly ask a question that is hard to answer: which AI systems do we run, who owns them, how were they tested and how do we know they still behave as intended.

pain_points.title: No complete inventory
pain_points.detail: Models built by data science, bought from vendors or embedded in SaaS tools sit in different registers, and some are in none.

pain_points.title: Evidence scattered across teams
pain_points.detail: Validation reports, data lineage, approval notes and monitoring dashboards live in separate folders and formats.

pain_points.title: Generative AI outside existing model policy
pain_points.detail: Policies written for scorecards do not say how to test or monitor a chatbot, a retrieval system or a vendor language model.

pain_points.title: Framework language that is hard to apply
pain_points.detail: Recommendations in RBI's FREE-AI framework, ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF must be translated into specific controls and artefacts.

solution.overview: We build the evidence pack with your risk, compliance and technology teams. First we discover and inventory AI systems through questionnaires, procurement and architecture records and interviews, and classify each by use, customer impact and risk tier. A document intelligence pipeline reads existing model documentation, validation reports, vendor contracts and policies, and maps what exists to a control set drawn from FREE-AI recommendations, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF and your model risk policy. Gaps are listed per system with an owner. Higher-risk generative AI systems receive targeted tests for leakage, bias and unsafe output, and the results join the pack. The output is a register your teams maintain.
capabilities: AI system discovery and inventory across in-house, vendor and embedded models
Risk tiering by use case, customer impact, autonomy and data sensitivity
Automated reading of model documents, validation reports and contracts against a control set
Control mapping to FREE-AI recommendations, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF and the bank's own policy
Targeted testing of higher-risk generative AI systems for leakage, bias and unsafe output
Gap register with owners, due dates and evidence links, exportable for audit

workflow.title: Agree the control set
workflow.detail: We combine your model risk policy with relevant framework recommendations into one control list approved by risk and compliance.

workflow.title: Discover AI systems
workflow.detail: Questionnaires, procurement and architecture records and interviews identify AI systems and their owners.

workflow.title: Collect and read evidence
workflow.detail: Existing documents are ingested and mapped to controls, each mapping linked to its source passage.

workflow.title: Tier and test
workflow.detail: Systems are risk-tiered, and higher-risk generative AI systems receive targeted tests.

workflow.title: Review gaps with owners
workflow.detail: Model owners and the model risk team confirm mappings and accept or dispute each gap.

workflow.title: Publish the pack
workflow.detail: The register, evidence links and gap plan go to the risk committee and internal audit.

inputs: Model risk management policy and any existing model inventory
Model documentation, validation and monitoring reports
Vendor contracts and AI-related due diligence responses
Access to test environments for higher-risk generative AI systems
outputs: AI system register with owners, purpose and risk tier
Control mapping with links to source evidence
Gap register with owners and due dates

human_in_the_loop: Model owners, the model risk team and compliance confirm every mapping and gap; the pipeline proposes and people decide. The risk committee owns risk acceptance, and the pack states plainly where evidence is missing.
guardrails: Every control mapping linked to the exact passage it relies on
Unsupported mappings recorded as gaps, never inferred
Confidential documents processed in the bank's environment with role-based access
Framework references described as alignment, not certification
Version history for the register and evidence pack
compliance_notes: Aligned with themes in RBI's FREE-AI framework (2025), a set of recommendations for responsible AI in financial services, and with ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF.
For EU-facing operations, helps prepare documentation expected under the EU AI Act, which treats credit scoring of individuals as high-risk.
Does not certify compliance; the bank's own assessment and its auditors decide.

pilot.scope: One business area, such as retail lending or digital channels, inventoried end to end, with evidence mapped for its AI systems and one generative AI system tested.
deliverables: AI system register for the pilot area
Control mapping and gap register with evidence links
Test report for one generative AI system
Plan and effort estimate for bank-wide roll-out

what_we_measure.how: AI systems found compared with those in existing registers, confirmed with business owners.
Control mappings accepted by owners and model risk as proposed, with changes or rejected.
Controls with linked evidence compared with controls applicable to each system's risk tier.
Gaps with an owner, due date and status, tracked through the pilot.

faqs.a: FREE-AI is a framework of recommendations released by RBI in 2025, not a binding regulation in itself. Many banks use it, alongside existing RBI directions on IT governance and outsourcing, to shape their AI policies and evidence.

faqs.q: Will this certify us against ISO/IEC 42001?
faqs.a: No. Certification is carried out by accredited certification bodies. Our work organises evidence and closes gaps, which helps if you choose to pursue certification later.
Yes. Vendor tools with embedded models are inventoried, contracts and due diligence responses are mapped to controls, and gaps such as missing testing rights are listed for procurement to address.
Documents are processed in your environment or a tenancy you control, with role-based access. The language models we use do not retain or train on your data.
